2609.18283.title: Where Should Agents Live? Energy-Memory Characterization of Agentic AI for the Edge-Cloud Continuum
2609.18283.paper_summary: As telecommunication networks evolve toward autonomous 5G-Advanced and 6G operations, agentic artificial intelligence (AI) workflows, where large language models (LLMs) execute multi-step reasoning, invoke diagnostic tools, retrieve domain knowledge, and coordinate across agent teams, are increasingly embedded across the edge-cloud continuum. While the biological brain accomplishes complex cognition on an exceptionally modest metabolic power budget of approximately 20W contemporary LLMs are profoundly energy- and memory-intensive, making sustainable lifecycle orchestration a critical operational priority. However, existing AI lifecycle metrics evaluate only isolated, single-model inferences or overlook multi-agent execution graphs entirely. Consequently, network operators lack foundational models to determine whether distributed agent communication incurs meaningful energy costs and where across edge-cloud tiers agent teams should physically reside. To address this gap, we introduce agentic-eCAL, generalizing the Energy Cost of AI Lifecycle (eCAL) metric to directed multi-agent workflows by coupling a closed-form two-rate single-call energy model (compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode) with 7-layer OSI data transport. Grounded in hundreds of GPU benchmark configurations on NVIDIA A100 and H100, 16 open-weight models and 8 orchestration topologies, we validate components of the metric and study workflow placement implications. Our findings demonstrate that inter-agent text transport incurs 0.25% of workflow energy across 5G RAN, metro, and optical links. Therefore in edge-cloud agent placement the dominant energy cost of distribution is often not the transmission of inter-agent text itself, but the additional inference and context processing induced by that communication.
2609.18283.paper_summary_zh: 隨著電信網絡向自主的5G-Advanced和6G運營演進，代理人工智慧（AI）工作流程日益嵌入邊緣雲端連續體中，這些工作流程中大型語言模型（LLMs）執行多步推理、調用診斷工具、檢索領域知識並協調代理團隊。雖然生物大腦在約20W的極其有限的代謝功率預算下完成複雜的認知，但當代的LLMs卻極其耗能和佔用記憶，使得可持續的生命周期協調成為一項關鍵的運營優先事項。然而，現有的AI生命周期指標僅評估孤立的單一模型推斷，或完全忽視多代理執行圖。結果，網絡運營商缺乏基礎模型來判斷分佈式代理通信是否產生了有意義的能量成本，以及代理團隊應該在邊緣雲端層次中實際位於何處。為了解決這一空白，我們引入了代理eCAL，將AI生命周期的能量成本（eCAL）指標推廣到定向多代理工作流程，通過將封閉形式的雙速單次調用能量模型（計算限制的預填充和記憶限制的解碼）與7層OSI數據傳輸相結合。基於數百個在NVIDIA A100和H100上的GPU基準配置、16個開放權重模型和8個協調拓撲，我們驗證了該指標的組件並研究了工作流程佈局的影響。我們的研究結果表明，代理間的文本傳輸在5G RAN、城市和光纖鏈路中佔據了工作流程能量的0.25%。因此，在邊緣雲端代理佈局中，分配的主要能量成本往往不是代理間文本本身的傳輸，而是由該通信引起的額外推斷和上下文處理。
